note: Proposed NEW JFR events derived from gap analysis of -Xlog log sites that no existing JFR event covers. These events DO NOT exist in the JDK 25 oracle (jfr metadata, 194 events); they are candidates for upstream proposal. Scope of this analysis: -Xlog:trimnative*,gc*,gc+region*,gc+ergo*,gc+humongous*,stringdedup*=info (127 uncovered firing sites). Each 'replaces' entry cites the HotSpot source file + verbatim log format string the event would make recoverable via JFR. Field types follow the oracle convention (long for time/bytes/counters, int for ids, float/double for ratios, boolean/String). startTime/duration follow the standard JFR event contract. Status note (2026-08-17): JDK 26 adds jdk.StringDeduplication (partial overlap — see rationale on StringDeduplicationStatistics). JDK 27 adds jdk.ShenandoahPromotionInformation (in metadata.xml, not yet released). JDK-8365306 (In Progress) will add a native-heap-trim JFR event. None of the other 9 proposed events have upstream work in progress.

proposed.label: String Deduplication Statistics
proposed.rationale: JDK 26 added jdk.StringDeduplication (JDK-8037914) with coarse counters (inspectedCount, deduplicatedCount, lastDeduplicated, totalDeduplicated). This per-cycle statistics summary event carries what the log line still emits but JDK 26's event does not: per-cycle new-unknown counts, byte totals (dedupedBytes, newUnknownBytes, totalDedupedBytes, totalNewUnknownBytes), and the deduplication ratio. Consider whether the remaining fields justify a second event or whether JDK 26's jdk.StringDeduplication should be extended instead.

replaces.logLine: Concurrent String Deduplication %zu (inspected), %zu/ (new unknown), %zu/ (deduped), total avg deduped/new unknown bytes ,  (total deduped), (total new unknown),  of

proposed.label: Shenandoah Card Statistics
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational remembered-set card scanning emits detailed per-worker and cumulative dirty/clean card statistics with no JFR event. workerId = -1 denotes the cumulative row.

replaces.logLine: Card stats: dirty %zu (max run: %zu), clean %zu (max run: %zu), dirty scans/objs %zu

proposed.label: Shenandoah Minimum Mutator Utilization
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah's MMU tracker prints GC utilization (GCU) and mutator utilization (MU) per phase increment with no JFR analogue. Directly parallels the existing jdk.GCCPUTime event but for Shenandoah mutator-utilization accounting.

replaces.logLine: At end of %s: GCU: %.1f%%, MU: %.1f%% for duration %.3fs (totals to be subsumed in next gc report)

proposed.label: Shenandoah Reclaim Progress
proposed.rationale: shenandoahMetrics.cpp's ShenandoahMetricsSnapshot::is_good_progress() evaluates free-space, used-space, internal fragmentation, and external fragmentation progress after each cycle and logs whether each dimension met its threshold. No JFR event carries this cross-dimension progress check. The event fires once per cycle with one row per dimension (dimension='free'/'used'/'internal-frag'/'external-frag').

proposed.label: ZGC NMethod Registration
proposed.rationale: ZGC periodically reports the count of registered vs unregistered nmethods. A clean 1:1 periodic snapshot with no existing event.

proposed.label: GC Overhead Limit Exceeded
proposed.rationale: Fires immediately before the JVM throws OutOfMemoryError: GC Overhead Limit exceeded. A high-signal failure moment that is currently invisible to JFR; complements jdk.OldObjectSample / jdk.AllocationRequiringGC narratives.

replaces.logLine: GC Overhead Limit exceeded too often (%zu).
GC Overhead Limit exceeded too often (%zu).

proposed.label: Native Heap Trim
proposed.rationale: The JVM periodically calls malloc_trim/madvise to return RSS to the OS after GC. The log line (trimNativeHeap.cpp) records before/after RSS and delta, but no JFR event carries this. Especially valuable on containerised deployments where RSS spikes are monitored closely. detailsAvailable=false when /proc/self/status is unavailable (non-Linux or restricted containers). JDK-8365306 (In Progress) confirms upstream interest: its design explicitly requests an event-driven trim event with 'when, how much RSS recovered, and duration'.

proposed.label: G1 Concurrent Refinement Cycle
proposed.rationale: G1's concurrent refinement thread sweeps dirty cards between pauses. The gc+refine and gc+ergo+refine log tags emit per-sweep card counts, thread counts, pending-card targets, and rate predictions with no JFR analogue. Currently only pause-level refined-cards totals appear in jdk.GCPhasePause. This event enables correlating refinement throughput with subsequent pause work. The key log line (g1ConcurrentRefine.cpp:612) shows: wanted threads, total pending, pending-from-gc, card stats, and timing sub-totals.

replaces.logLine: Concurrent refinement: wanted %u, pending cards target %zu, predicted refine rate %.2f, dirtied card rate %.2f, goal %.2fms%s

proposed.label: ZGC Director Rule Evaluation
proposed.rationale: ZGC's director evaluates up to seven heuristic rules each cycle (Timer, AllocationRate, HighUsage, Warmup, Proactive, SoftReference, NMethodFlush) to decide whether to trigger GC. The gc+director log tag records per-rule evaluation with context data (allocation rate, free bytes, time estimates). No JFR event exposes this decision logic; correlating GC triggers with allocation pressure, cycle timing, or free-space thresholds is impossible without log parsing. generation='Minor'/'Major' matches ZGC's generational terminology from the log prefix 'Rule Minor:' / 'Rule Major:'. Sparse fields (e.g. maxAllocRate) are zero/NaN for rules that don't evaluate them.

replaces.logLine: Rule: Allocation Rate, Max Alloc Rate: %.1fMB/s, Free: %zuMB, GC time: %.3fs, Alloc time: %.3fs, Triggered: %s

proposed.label: Parallel GC Adaptive Size Policy
proposed.rationale: Parallel GC's AdaptiveSizePolicy runs a feedback loop after each GC to resize eden and survivor spaces toward throughput and pause-time goals. The gc+ergo log tag emits the full policy state (throughput/pause deltas, promotion rate, overflow flag, desired sizes) but no JFR event captures this. Understanding why generation sizes oscillate or GC overhead increases currently requires log parsing.

replaces.logLine: Adaptive: throughput: %.3f, pause: %.1f ms, gc-distance: %.3f (%.3f) s, promoted: %.1f %s (%.1f %s), promotion-rate: %.1f M/s (%.1f M/s), overflowing: %s

proposed.label: Shenandoah Collection Decision
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational mode runs a regulator/control FSM that decides each cycle whether to collect young, old, or global, whether to run a mixed collection, and whether to interrupt/resume/cancel an in-progress cycle. This high-level decision is spread across shenandoahRegulatorThread.cpp, shenandoahGenerationalControlThread.cpp, shenandoahOldHeuristics.cpp with no JFR event. The mixedCandidates, mixedRegionsSelected, and oldEvacuationBudget fields come from shenandoahOldHeuristics.cpp's choose_collection_set_from_regiondata(). Note: adaptive heuristic z-score and margin-of-error are computed in should_start_gc() before the regulator accepts the request; they belong in a separate jdk.ShenandoahAdaptiveTrigger event rather than here.

replaces.logLine: Regulator decided to start a GC cycle
Old-gen is planning to %s its collection set from %u/%u candidate regions
